solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Artful, perhaps, condescending to eat seconds

indicators.note: something that eats another word takes it inside, so the word for condescending swallows the letter

parts.note: deigning is condescending to do something

explanation.surface: Someone sly, perhaps, graciously agreeing to tuck into second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' belongs with the definition: being artful is one example of being scheming.
explanation.definitionFit: A designing person is crafty and scheming, as an artful one is; the 'perhaps' marks it as an illustrative synonym.

clue.text: Please take a chair, to accept record down-payment

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the polite invitation to be seated holds the record inside it

parts.note: an invitation to be seated, 'do sit'
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A salesperson seats a customer and takes a note of the first payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is a first part-payment made to secure a purchase, which is a down-payment.

clue.text: Newly risen, eating a snack

indicators.note: the rearranged letters eat, or take inside, the single letter
made newly means put into a fresh form, so these five letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone just out of bed having a quick bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly' rearranges RISEN to SRNIE; 'eating' puts A inside it after the S. SARNIE is British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarnie is an informal British word for a sandwich, a typical light snack.

clue.text: Boss shortly makes a mistake

indicators.note: said shortly, the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: gaffer is British informal for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: A curt manager slips up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims the last letter, R, from GAFFER, a British word for a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder or embarrassing error, a synonym for a mistake.

clue.text: Why in bed, needing tablet first off?

indicators.note: with the first letter taken off, the word for a tablet loses its opening letter

parts.note: a pill is a medicinal tablet

explanation.surface: Asking why someone is laid up and wants a pill before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' removes P from PILL. The definition is cryptic: being sick is the reason for lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sick is the explanation for someone staying in bed, so the reason stands for the state.

clue.text: Make too much fuss, leaving trench?

definitions.meaning: in First World War slang, soldiers climbing out of the trenches to attack

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to act excessively, and literally described soldiers climbing over the trench parapet to advance.

clue.text: Extremely restless in misery is not so good

indicators.note: the pair of outer letters go in the word for misery

parts.note: woe is misery or sorrow

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Being unable to settle when already unhappy only makes things worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives RS, the end letters of 'restless', which go 'in' WOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Worse is the comparative of bad, meaning less good, which is what not so good says.

clue.text: Article in wood is soft? That's an illusion

indicators.note: the article goes in the wood, splitting it before its final letter

parts.note: willow is a wood, used for cricket bats
the is the definite article
p is piano, the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: Wondering if a piece of timber is really soft, or only seems so.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'soft' is not a texture here but the musical direction piano, while 'in' splits the wood just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsh light that lures travellers is proverbially something deceptive, a delusive hope or phantom.

clue.text: Concerned with doctor and examination, most faint

parts.note: re means about or concerning
MO is a medical officer
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: A patient worried about a medical check-up, almost fainting.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote can mean slight, as in a remote chance, so its superlative means faintest.

clue.text: Left book showing responsibilities of minister

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a folio is a large book

explanation.surface: A minister leaves behind a volume describing official duties.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's portfolio is the set of departmental duties held in government.

clue.text: Dance round on leg perhaps

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another is placed after it

parts.note: a leg is an example of a limb
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A dancer spinning on one leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbo is a West Indian dance in which one bends backwards under a lowered bar.

clue.text: As plaything, order calculator

parts.note: a slide is a piece of playground equipment
to rule is to order or command

explanation.surface: Ordering a calculator to be treated as a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A slide rule is a pre-electronic calculating device with sliding logarithmic scales.

clue.text: Wave almost unwarranted, not in time

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: undue means unwarranted or excessive
late means not on time

explanation.surface: A late arrival's wave that is hardly justified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last E from UNDUE, leaving UNDU.
explanation.definitionFit: To undulate is to move with a wavelike motion, so the verb wave fits.

clue.text: Versailles, for example, compact

definitions.meaning: the 1919 peace settlement signed at Versailles
as a noun, a formal agreement

explanation.walkthrough: 'compact' reads as an adjective but is the noun for an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Versailles settlement was a formal agreement between nations, and a compact is such an agreement.

clue.text: Believe notice about newspaper chief

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it, so the review wraps the editor

parts.note: a crit is a critical notice or review
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Trusting a review written about the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a story is to accept it as true, a synonym of believe.

clue.text: Dost thou rate as most highly disagreeable?

definitions.meaning: the archaic second-person form of the verb rank, to rate or grade
superlative of rank, meaning foul or offensive

explanation.definitionFit: Rank means foul-smelling or offensive, so its superlative is the most disagreeable; and 'thou rankest' is old English for 'you rate'.

clue.text: A rule for entering fast road in the country

indicators.note: the piece going in enters the road, sitting between its two characters

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, read here as MI
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A regulation about joining a motorway somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway, with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in south-east Africa, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Consider goin' in to accept thanks

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the clipped phrase holds the word for thanks

parts.note: entering with its final g dropped, as the apostrophe in goin' signals
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone dropping their g's while thinking of going inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in goin' says the matching word loses its G: ENTERIN'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain an idea is to consider it or hold it in the mind.

clue.text: Member of this family finds Republican not initially faithful

indicators.note: without its initial letter, the word for faithful loses its first letter

parts.note: loyal means faithful

explanation.surface: A republican discovers a relative who was disloyal from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' removes L from LOYAL. The definition points to the family in the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal is a member of a king's or queen's family, so the noun fits.

clue.text: Snake: lifeboat turns back with it

indicators.note: turning back means reading the word for the boat in reverse

parts.note: Noah's ark saved its passengers from the flood

explanation.surface: A snake rides a lifeboat that heads back to shore.
explanation.definitionFit: The krait is a highly venomous Asian snake, so an example of the class.

clue.text: Ace inn, say, demolished regardless

indicators.note: a building demolished is broken up, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A first-rate pub knocked down whatever anyone says.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means whatever happens or anyway, a synonym of regardless.

clue.text: Girl takes a couple of notes

parts.note: N is short for note, so two of them give NN

explanation.surface: A girl jots down a couple of memos.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann is a girl's name, and crossword setters use any first name to mean girl or boy.

clue.text: Old Prime Minister's gone back … to this?

indicators.note: going back means reading the possessive name from end to start

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was British Prime Minister in the 1830s and 1840s

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a long-dead statesman has drifted off to his rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone back' reverses PEELS. The definition joins the clue: having 'gone to' slumber.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has 'gone to' it is asleep, so the slumber is what the old statesman has gone to.

clue.text: I plan, lest ordered to be participant in quiz show

indicators.note: put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone arranging plans to be on a TV quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: A panellist is a member of a panel, such as the team on a television quiz programme.
